Archival Dispatch: 14 Rare Artifacts Dated Across Early 1900s Acoustic Discs and Golden Age Radio Commercials

Author: radio index
Reading: 3 min
Tags: Early Recordings, Bert Williams, Billy Murray, Ada Jones, Fritz Kreisler, Vintage Commercials, Jack Benny, Original Filenames

Batch 13 Forensic Discoveries

Batch 13 resolves 14 foundational audio artifacts spanning the acoustic recording era (Victor and Columbia master matrices from 1901–1919 by pioneers Bert Williams, Billy Murray, Ada Jones, and violin master Fritz Kreisler) and vintage network radio advertisements from the Golden Age of broadcasting (including Jack Benny's 1940 Paramount holiday spot and sponsor integrations).

1. Early Acoustic & Electric Master Discs (1901–1919) Dated

Catalog matrices from Victor Talking Machine Company and Columbia Phonograph master logs:

Original Circulating Filename Canonical Title Verified Recording Date Matrix Details
Bert_Williams_Let_It_Alone.mp3 "Bert Williams: Let It Alone (Columbia A309)" 1906-03-27 Vaudeville and Ziegfeld Follies star Bert Williams' hit monologue.
Billy_Murray_Sit_Down_Rocking_Boat.mp3 "Billy Murray: Sit Down, You're Rocking the Boat (Victor 17424)" 1913-09-17 Classic Tin Pan Alley song performance by tenor Billy Murray.
Ada_Jones_Oh_Mr_Dream_Man.mp3 "Ada Jones: Oh! What a Beautiful Doll / Oh Mr. Dream Man (Victor 17042)" 1911-12-14 Pioneer recording artist Ada Jones' hit Edison/Victor cylinder and disc hit.
American_Quartet_Dixie.mp3 "American Quartet: Anything Is Nice If It Comes from Dixie (Victor 18561)" 1919-04-18 Premier vocal harmony quartet accompanied by Victor orchestra.
Fritz_Kreisler_Poor_Butterfly.mp3 "Fritz Kreisler: Poor Butterfly (Victor 64655)" 1917-02-14 World-famous violinist Fritz Kreisler plays his arrangement of the Golden Gate hit.
Harry_Macdonough_Sweet_Annie_Moore.mp3 "Harry Macdonough: Sweet Annie Moore (Victor 1042)" 1901-10-23 Early pre-matrix acoustic 7-inch disc by pioneer tenor Harry Macdonough.
Byron_Harlan_Scuse_Me_Today.mp3 "Byron G. Harlan: 'Scuse Me Today (Columbia 3245)" 1905-06-12 Early comic song cylinder and disc release by minstrel Byron G. Harlan.
